title: By 15 months, most children look at a familiar object when it is named
summary: The CDC says that by 15 months, most children look at a familiar object when you name it.
body: On the 15-month page, under language and communication, the CDC lists looking at a familiar object when you name it. The item is about matching a spoken name to a thing the child already knows. It is one US checklist line for most children by 15 months. It is not a vocabulary score.

sources.title: Milestones by 15 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US CDC page, public domain. Updated and reviewed 16 May 2026. Supports the language item 'Looks at a familiar object when you name it.'
